original: Validate every phase against real data before moving to the next — synthetic tests pass when the real thing fails because mocks diverge from production behavior
rewritten: Before moving to the next implementation phase: validate the current phase against real data — synthetic tests pass when the real thing fails because mocks diverge from production

original: Establish baseline metrics before implementing any improvement — without before/after numbers you cannot distinguish real improvement from noise
rewritten: Before implementing any improvement or optimization: establish baseline metrics first — without before/after numbers you cannot distinguish real improvement from noise

original: Update CLAUDE.md when project structure, architecture, or conventions change — without this, the next session starts with stale context and makes wrong assumptions
rewritten: After changing project structure, architecture, or conventions: update CLAUDE.md — without this, the next session starts with stale context and makes wrong assumptions

original: Review PRDs with multiple specialist subagents (architect, security, database, code quality) in parallel — a single reviewer misses entire categories of issues that other specialists catch immediately
rewritten: When reviewing a PRD or design document: use multiple specialist subagents (architect, security, code quality) in parallel — a single reviewer misses entire categories of issues

original: Keep running review rounds until two consecutive rounds produce zero CRITICAL, HIGH, or MEDIUM findings — fixed round counts stop too early when issues cascade, and too late when code is already clean
rewritten: After each review round: keep running until two consecutive rounds produce zero CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings — fixed round counts stop too early or too late

original: Search GitHub for existing implementations and proven patterns before writing anything from scratch — 80% of problems are already solved, and battle-tested code has fewer bugs than fresh code
rewritten: Before writing new utility code or implementing a common pattern: search GitHub first — 80% of problems are already solved with battle-tested code

original: Fix the pipeline stage that produces bad output, do not patch downstream — downstream patches accumulate into unmaintainable complexity while the root cause keeps generating bad data
rewritten: When debugging poor output quality: fix the upstream pipeline stage, not downstream patches — downstream fixes accumulate into unmaintainable complexity

original: Each pipeline stage must be independently high quality — relying on downstream stages to rescue upstream failures means any stage failure cascades through the entire system
rewritten: When building multi-stage pipelines: ensure each stage is independently high quality — downstream stages cannot rescue upstream failures

original: If a tool call or LLM response takes 10x longer than expected, investigate immediately — normalized slowness compounds across thousands of calls into hours of wasted time
rewritten: When a tool call or LLM response takes 10x longer than expected: investigate immediately — normalized slowness compounds across thousands of calls

original: Never trust LLM-generated confidence scores — use evidence counts, ensemble agreement, or historical track record instead, because LLMs produce plausible numbers that are poorly calibrated and create false certainty
rewritten: When an LLM outputs confidence scores or probabilities: don't trust them — use evidence counts, ensemble agreement, or track record instead

original: Spike-test risky integrations before building on them — if a dependency is unvalidated (new library, untested API, custom wrapper), spend 2 hours proving it works before designing an architecture around it, because discovering it fails after building 3 layers on top wastes days
rewritten: Before building on an unvalidated dependency: spike-test it for 2 hours — discovering a library fails after building 3 layers on top wastes days

original: Prefer mature extensible frameworks over building from scratch — if LangGraph, FastAPI, or similar battle-tested projects provide the feature (routing, checkpointing, streaming), use them even if a simpler stdlib approach works today, because refactoring from simple to framework later costs more than starting with the framework
rewritten: When choosing between a simple stdlib approach and a framework (LangGraph, FastAPI): prefer the framework — refactoring from simple to framework later costs more

original: Reuse popular open-source components for each layer of the system — only build custom code for what doesn't exist, because mature projects provide stability, community support, and extensibility that hand-rolled code cannot match
rewritten: When building system components: reuse popular open-source projects — only build custom code for what doesn't exist; mature projects provide stability and community support

original: Always test with real external data after mocked tests pass — NaN values, missing columns, empty strings, and API format differences only surface with live data, never with synthetic fixtures
rewritten: After mocked tests pass: test with real external data — NaN values, missing columns, and API format differences only surface with live data

original: Set subagent scope boundaries and terminate stale agents — an unbounded reviewer will find infinite speculative findings in any document, consuming context without improving quality
rewritten: When launching subagents: set explicit scope boundaries and kill stale ones — unbounded reviewers find infinite speculative findings

original: Audit your ground truth before blaming the model — wrong test expectations and fixture errors are indistinguishable from model failures, and removing wrong expectations is a free quality improvement with zero code change
rewritten: When model predictions look wrong: audit the ground truth first — wrong fixture expectations are indistinguishable from model failures, and removing them is a free quality improvement

original: Write rules and instructions that explain consequences, not just commands — agents follow rules they understand ("without Enter, text is never submitted") but ignore rules that just say what to do ("always send Enter")
rewritten: When writing rules or instructions for agents: explain consequences, not just commands — agents follow rules they understand but ignore rules that just say what to do

original: Control your evaluation methodology before trusting results — if you benchmark model A against model B's artifacts, model B wins by default; always evaluate the full pipeline end-to-end with each model generating its own inputs
rewritten: Before trusting benchmark results: verify the evaluation methodology — if you benchmark model A against model B's artifacts, model B wins by default

original: Run convergence reviews (code + security agents in parallel) after each implementation milestone — a single end-of-project review misses bugs that compound across phases, while per-phase reviews catch them when they're cheap to fix
rewritten: After each implementation milestone: run convergence reviews with parallel code + security agents — per-phase reviews catch bugs when they're cheap to fix

original: Run convergence reviews on PRD changes too, not just code — a design gap that survives review becomes an implementation bug that survives testing, because every downstream artifact inherits upstream ambiguity
rewritten: After revising a PRD or design document: run convergence reviews — design gaps that survive review become implementation bugs that survive testing

original: After each milestone, create a comprehensive test plan before testing — the test plan itself should be reviewed by subagents (architect for coverage gaps, security for attack vectors, code quality for edge cases) because an incomplete test plan produces false confidence
rewritten: Before testing a completed milestone: create a comprehensive test plan reviewed by subagents — an incomplete test plan produces false confidence

original: Follow the three-layer quality gate: PRD + reviews → Implementation + reviews → Test plan + reviews — skipping any layer compounds risk; a reviewed PRD catches design gaps, reviewed code catches bugs, a reviewed test plan catches blind spots that both missed
rewritten: For any significant feature: follow the three-layer gate — PRD + reviews, then implementation + reviews, then test plan + reviews — skipping any layer compounds risk

original: Put reasoning BEFORE decision in LLM JSON output format — when the signal/action field comes first, the model commits to a default (e.g. "hold") before thinking; when reasoning comes first, the model analyzes the data and makes an informed decision, producing dramatically better outputs without needing thinking mode
rewritten: When choosing LLM reasoning mode: thinking mode costs 10x but is most decisive; reasoning-first JSON recovers 80% of quality at 3x speed — match compute to difficulty

original: Use "reasoning-first" JSON: {"reasoning": "...", "signal": "..."} not {"signal": "...", "reasoning": "..."} — field order in JSON prompts determines whether the model thinks before deciding; this is the cheapest quality upgrade available
rewritten: Use "reasoning-first" JSON: {"reasoning": "...", "signal": "..."} not {"signal": "...", "reasoning": "..."} — field order in JSON prompts determines whether the model thinks before deciding; this is the cheapest quality upgrade available

original: Thinking mode (hidden CoT) produces the most decisive outputs but costs 10x tokens and time — reasoning-first JSON format recovers 80% of the quality at 3x the speed; use thinking for live analysis, reasoning-first for backtesting
rewritten: When choosing LLM reasoning mode: thinking mode costs 10x but is most decisive; reasoning-first JSON recovers 80% of quality at 3x speed — match compute to difficulty

original: Always include an example JSON object in the prompt — models that see the exact format they should produce have near-zero parse errors; without an example, they improvise with markdown fences and free text
rewritten: Always include an example JSON object in the prompt — models that see the exact format they should produce have near-zero parse errors; without an example, they improvise with markdown fences and free text

original: Classify every task as SIMPLE, MEDIUM, or COMPLEX before starting — state the assessment explicitly with reasoning
rewritten: Classify every task as SIMPLE, MEDIUM, or COMPLEX before starting — state the assessment explicitly with reasoning

original: SIMPLE tasks (1-2 files, low risk) can proceed without a plan — just implement and verify
rewritten: When receiving a task touching 1-2 files (config change, small fix): proceed without a plan — simple tasks don't need overhead

original: MEDIUM tasks (3-10 files) require an inline plan, research, tests alongside code, and agent review after implementation
rewritten: When receiving a task touching 3-10 files: create an inline plan with research, write tests alongside code, and run agent review after — medium tasks need structure

original: COMPLEX tasks (10+ files, architecture changes) require a full PRD written to artifacts/ before any implementation begins
rewritten: When receiving a task touching 10+ files or requiring new architecture: write a full PRD first — complex tasks without specs produce rework and missed requirements

original: Use the planner agent for complex features, architect agent for system design decisions, tdd-guide agent for new features and bug fixes
rewritten: When starting complex features: use the planner agent; for system design: use architect; for new features/bugs: use tdd-guide — match the agent to the task type

original: Launch parallel subagents for independent review tasks — never run them sequentially when they can run simultaneously
rewritten: When multiple independent review or analysis tasks exist: launch parallel subagents — sequential execution wastes time when tasks don't depend on each other

original: Run code review with 3 parallel agents (code-reviewer, security-reviewer, python-reviewer) and iterate until clean
rewritten: After writing code: run 3 parallel review agents (code-reviewer, security-reviewer, python-reviewer) and iterate until clean

original: Run iterative PRD reviews until a round comes back clean — typical convergence is 4 rounds
rewritten: When reviewing PRDs: iterate rounds with specialist agents until a round comes back clean — each round finds issues at a different depth

original: Manually inspect LLM output after every classification wave — read actual output, do not trust confidence scores
rewritten: Manually inspect LLM output after every classification wave — read actual output, do not trust confidence scores

original: Never trust small sample benchmark results — run the full dataset before drawing conclusions
rewritten: Never trust small sample benchmark results — run the full dataset before drawing conclusions

original: Never build infrastructure around unproven techniques — test hypotheses in controlled experiments first, implement only winners
rewritten: Never build infrastructure around unproven techniques — test hypotheses in controlled experiments first, implement only winners

original: Use lightweight deterministic approaches first, add LLM stages only when they demonstrably improve quality
rewritten: Use lightweight deterministic approaches first, add LLM stages only when they demonstrably improve quality

original: Store all predictions, reasoning, and grounding in benchmark results for later reanalysis — not just numeric scores
rewritten: When saving benchmark results: store predictions, reasoning, and grounding — not just numeric scores — for later reanalysis when methodology changes

original: Filter pipeline noise at multiple independent stages with configurable thresholds — no single filter point
rewritten: When building retrieval pipelines: filter noise at multiple independent stages with configurable thresholds — no single filter point can handle all query types

original: When schema or cardinality changes, audit every consumer (views, queries, CLI, exports, tests) before implementing
rewritten: When schema or cardinality changes, audit every consumer (views, queries, CLI, exports, tests) before implementing

original: Before compaction, save task state to artifacts/ including what was done, what remains, key decisions, and blockers
rewritten: Before compaction, save task state to artifacts/ including what was done, what remains, key decisions, and blockers

original: When running A/B benchmark comparisons on LLM artifacts, use the same pre-built artifact and change only one variable
rewritten: When running A/B benchmark comparisons on LLM artifacts, use the same pre-built artifact and change only one variable

original: Run the original paper code first when reproducing published results — do not theorize about score gaps without evidence
rewritten: When reproducing published results: run the original paper code first — do not theorize about score gaps without evidence from the reference implementation

original: Score gaps between models on routine tasks usually indicate code or config differences, not model quality differences
rewritten: Score gaps between models on routine tasks usually indicate code or config differences, not model quality differences

original: After 2 failed fix attempts on the same error, stop and ask the user for guidance instead of spiraling
rewritten: After 2 failed fix attempts on the same error, stop and ask the user for guidance instead of spiraling
